Morning procedures for pet arrivals for new staff
New handlers should know a habit of care

This page matters because the first contact at arrival pickup sets the whole tone for the trip. You are the face of Aurelia Skyways when travelers are tired, pets are anxious, and every detail has to land cleanly. Keep your voice calm, keep your hands ready, and keep your notes tight. The Companion Animal Travel Desk runs on quick checks, clear handoffs, and steady follow-through, so do not drift or guess.

When a carrier comes in, look for label match, secure latches, and visible comfort signs before anything moves. Keep the path clear and stay alert for extra support from the ground team, because loose handling creates delays and stress fast. If a traveler seems unsure, speak in plain language and keep the next step short. The senior coordinator handles daily service decisions, and you must route problems upward without waiting for them to grow. <<FACT F107>> Do not improvise on escalation, and do not send anyone away with a half-finished handoff.

After the initial check, stay focused on the pickup flow. <<FACT F101>> Confirm paperwork against the carrier tag, then pass the case forward with the right note in the service record. If Murphy or another pet shows signs of distress, lower your voice, slow your movements, and give the traveler a simple update without crowding them. Never leave a carrier unattended, even for a quick second, and never assume someone else has already handled the next step.

Keep your language direct, kind, and actionable. Say what you see, say what happens next, and avoid extra talk that can confuse a traveler in a hurry. If a carrier needs special attention, flag it right away and make sure the handoff is clean. What to remember is simple: steady care, clear escalation, and a clean pickup protect the pet and the traveler every time.
